  • Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

Sources indicate that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

Industry observers note that hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

Recent findings suggest that you can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

In a recent development, stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

According to recent reports, despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

Industry observers note that I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

Industry observers note that even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

Recent findings suggest that there are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

Industry observers note that for breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

Industry observers note that if you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

According to recent reports, for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

You can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

Sources indicate that one of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

Industry observers note that the family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

Sources indicate that next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

It has been revealed that one of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

Industry observers note that if you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set new limits on screenshots.
  • Whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers.
  • Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set new limits on screenshots. The company will prevent screenshotting in its iOS 27 app and “when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android,” Signal President Meredith Whittaker wrote in a blog post Friday.

Whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers. These features observe what’s on a user’s screen as context for completing requests.

Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.

Recent findings suggest that “Your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” Whittaker said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

Signal also blocked screenshots last year in response to Microsoft’s controversial Recall AI feature, which could capture screenshots of Signal chats on devices running Windows 11.

In a recent development, signal’s move is another reminder of how Substantial Tech’s AI strategy trickles downstream. As AI features have moved from services external to the OS (like chatbots from OpenAI or Anthropic) to further inside of it, third-party apps have to adapt to conditions that undermine their hard-won privacy infrastructure.

Also: How I use Meta Muse safely to stretch my AI budget – and what I never let it do.

Just last week, researchers at Google DeepMind used AI agents to formally verify Signal’s code, building on Signal’s own work to essentially prove the app’s encryption works. That’s a high bar for a security guarantee within the app, but it becomes meaningless if an agent can simply grab messages off a screen.

Samsung is reportedly working on its own agent, Galaxy Claw, and Apple is developing a rival for Claude and ChatGPT as well.

Whittaker noted Signal’s screenshot restriction isn’t perfect, saying that AI agents can still access app data through other means, “such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.” Earlier this week, a Reuters investigation supported by Signal and the AI Now Institute found that Meta’s Muse AI agent was using permissions from its initial setup in unexpected ways to access apps and data that a user had not explicitly connected it to.

Signal remarked its protections don’t at the moment work on MacOS.

“It is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” she added. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience.”.

If you’d still like to take screenshots, you can simply disable the setting, though Signal’s announcement strongly advised against it.

“Doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees,” Whittaker said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices.

Sources indicate that if you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being retired, and current consumers will lose access to both next year.

Industry observers note that all Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant.

Recent findings suggest that the change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.”.

Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

Google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app.

It has been revealed that as part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch.

Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

In a recent development, google claims that, in addition to devices automatically appearing in the Favorites tab in the Google Home app, you should be able to see camera views faster and access the most-used controls the moment you open the app. Part of the goal is to give consumers the latest security protections and cyber defenses, as well as Google Account security, privacy controls and threat protections –- all things that seem extra relevant these days as major companies across the US seem to be experiencing outages.

However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser.

You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

On Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed.

For most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027.

Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

The other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the company starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

Recent findings suggest that google notes Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and consumers will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information.

Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

Gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google declared earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. Customers in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now.

According to recent reports, on your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

It has been revealed that netflix (NFLX -2.96%) has Michael Burry's attention. Just not at today's price.

According to recent reports, that's a long way down. Netflix shares closed at $58.46 on Thursday, Nov. 19, their lowest close since May 2024 (using split-adjusted prices, because Netflix did a 10-for-1 stock split in November 2025).

With the stock trading near $58 as of this writing, a price in the high $30s would cut about another third off the shares.

I don't think investors have to wait for that. At today's price, Netflix already looks cheap for a tech giant whose profits are still climbing.

It has been revealed that michael Burry. Image source: Getty Images.

It has been revealed that burry has been circling Netflix for months. In July, he figured that Netflix at $67.75 per share traded at about 1.6 times its intrinsic value, which comes out to a value of roughly $42 a share by his math. He also said then that the stock would have to drop to the low $50s to get closer to an ideal buying opportunity.

So, the high $30s isn't a random number. It would let him buy under his own estimate of what the firm is worth.

Industry observers note that his concern is how long Netflix's content keeps its value. In July, he compared the streaming giant to Walt Disney and its Pixar studio, whose content he called evergreen. Much of what Netflix makes, he suggested, is OK for now but doesn't improve with age.

Industry observers note that sure, that's a fair worry about any business built on hit shows. But it's a long-term debate. In the meantime, Netflix's profits keep growing, making the high $30s look like a really pessimistic price.

Call the high $30s $38 a share. On average, analysts expect Netflix to earn about $3.80 per share in 2027, so a $38 stock would cost about 10 times next year's expected earnings. At around $58, shares trade at about 15 times next year's expected earnings.

By comparison, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) traded at 17.7 times its expected earnings for the next 12 months on Nov. 5, according to FactSet.

Remarked another way, Netflix stock already costs less than the average stock relative to its earnings. Burry's price would put it at a discount of over 40% to the market's price-to-earnings ratio.

It has been revealed that for $38 to be a market-average price, Netflix would have to earn only about $2.15 per share. It earned $2.53 per share in 2025 (split-adjusted too), and its earnings per share have grown year over year in every quarter of 2026 so far.

The high $30s would only make sense, then, if Netflix's profits were about to shrink.

It has been revealed that they don't look close to shrinking. Netflix's operating margin was 26.7% in 2024 and 29.5% in 2025, and the business is targeting 31.5% for 2026. Its third-quarter operating margin hit 34.6%. And management is guiding for a 26% margin in the fourth quarter, above the 24.5% Netflix reported a year before, even with costs from newly revealed job cuts. All told, Netflix states its outlook implies operating income growth of over 20% this year.

According to recent reports, also, Netflix keeps returning cash to shareholders. It spent $4.8 billion buying back its own stock in the third quarter alone, and it still had $22.3 billion in repurchase authorizations left.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Sales growth, though, keeps slowing. Revenue growth has fallen every quarter this year, to 11.8% year over year in the third quarter from 16.2% in the first. And management expects around 11.5% for the fourth quarter, while it has lowered its 2026 ad revenue outlook to about $2.7 billion from about $3 billion.

But a business still growing sales by double digits while raising its operating margin looks unlikely to wind up earning less than it did in 2025.

Could Burry still get his price? He might. Netflix stock is already down over half from its June 2025 record, and a stock that's fallen this far can keep falling.

Recent findings suggest that but waiting for the high $30s is arguably a bet that Netflix's earnings stall. At around 15 times next year's expected earnings, Netflix stock already prices in a lot of caution, I think. I'd consider buying shares now rather than waiting for Burry's number.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is not your parents’ Google home page.
  • Industry observers note that the upcoming elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm.
  • The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is not your parents’ Google home page. In its push to get more users to adopt its AI tools, the search engine giant is rolling out a raft of newly introduced features worldwide.

Industry observers note that the upcoming elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm. The Google Search button is gone, but the I’m Feeling Lucky button remains.

The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile. I was able to see the new buttons when signed in to my Google account.

When signed out, I was only able to see the typical home page, with the only AI button being AI Mode, which has been there since May 2025.

Recent findings suggest that clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a newly introduced page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. It’s the same image-generation tool you can use on other Google platforms such as the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and AI Mode in Search.

Clicking “Ask about files” allows for several options. You can have the AI analyze a document and rewrite it, simply have it answer questions or ask it to perform tasks such as “polish my resume” or “draft an email with action items.”.

The “Brainstorm” button prompts you to “describe your goal,” such as making a to-do list, learning how to code or finding a table at a restaurant.

Another new feature, as unveiled by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which indicates your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:.

Stein stated the fresh sidebar will help users go back to where they left off.

“People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.

I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.

Google will use your AI searches — whether they are questions, tasks, uploaded files or image generation — to train its AI models, but you can tell Google you’re opting out. CNET has an overview of how to tell chatbots not to use your data. Still, for Google specifically, you can go to Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity to turn off AI training.

Google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google announced several other newly introduced AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.

Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion users in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the manufacturer’s “fastest growing product ever.”.

But Google’s rush to force-feed AI into its products has met with plenty of pushback. The Upcoming York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts stated they might choose different search engines because Google said it will not remove AI from search tools used by students, The New York Times reported.

Google said search and the Gemini app will be turned off for schools unless school administrators want them. But Google said there will not be a chatbot-free version of search available for schools. So schools declining AI will not be able to search using Google at all.

It has been revealed that google’s AI Overviews, which appear at the top of many search page results, have also been blamed for a steep drop in web traffic to content publishers. AI Overviews summarize user search queries and replace the long list of blue hyperlinks that once appeared across search pages. So instead of clicking on those links to get more information, giving publishers valuable clicks, a user can simply get their query response by reading the AI Overview.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hyundai pulled back the cover on the newly introduced 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class.
  • Sources indicate that the humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand.
  • The updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai pulled back the cover on the newly introduced 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

Sources indicate that the humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

The updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

It has been revealed that an updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a new Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

Sharing the stage in LA, the newly introduced nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

Inside, a newly introduced cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

In a recent development, pleos Connect, Hyundai’s upcoming Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is said to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

It has been revealed that the Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s fresh AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai indicates the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

According to recent reports, “Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” stated Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the fresh Elantra is anything but bland.

In a recent development, the sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent upcoming SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

Recent findings suggest that the sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai says the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

Industry observers note that hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

According to recent reports, editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

By Jennifer Saibil – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:33PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Realty Income ›.

It has been revealed that if you're looking for a dividend stock, Realty Income (O +0.64%) is one of the best. It's a real estate investment trust (REIT), a business structure for real estate companies that pays out 90% of income as dividends, which is why REITs are often on best-dividend-stock lists.

Realty Income has an excellent track record, a high yield, and plenty of reasons to be confident about its future success. If you invest $10,000 right now, here's how much you can expect to get in dividends in 2027.

Realty Income has supported its top dividend by running a massive real estate business that leases properties to large essential retailers. These are chains you know and love and likely shop at, like Walmart (WMT +1.51%), Home Depot (HD +0.70%), 7-Eleven, and Dollar General (DG -2.23%).

Recent findings suggest that these are stores with well-established brands and strong cash flow, making them reliable renters. They have multi-year leases, some as long as 20 years, and Realty Income's occupancy rate is a high 98.8%. It has maintained a rate between 97% and 99% since 2000.

Recent findings suggest that grocery and convenience stores make up almost 20% of the portfolio, providing a resilient revenue stream, but the organization has also branched out into other areas as it expands and diversifies. The U.K. is one of its largest markets today, accounting for more than 15% of total properties, and Wynn Resorts (WYNN -2.07%) has become one of its biggest customers. Industrials make up a healthy 17% of the portfolio, and Realty Income is also getting started in data centers, which make up 1%.

Industry observers note that the company has more than 15,500 properties in 96 industries, and it's always buying fresh properties to keep growing. It has a $5.5 billion revolving credit facility, and it's raised more than $2 billion so far this year from various sources. It has a large pipeline of quality properties to choose from, and expanding beyond retail offers it more opportunities.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Realty Income has paid a dividend monthly for the past 677 months, or more than 56 years. It's one of the few dividend stocks that cuts you a check every month.

It also raises its dividend quarterly rather than annually, which is unusual among great dividend stocks. It has raised the dividend for the past 117 quarters, or more than 29 years.

At the current price, the dividend yields 5.6%, an excellent yield for a reliable dividend stock.

Realty Income is a dividend play, and the stock hasn't changed much over the past 10 years. However, now has been a particularly challenging time for the firm as interest and mortgage rates remain high.

Since its business model involves borrowing lots of money, higher interest rates mean it has to pay more to service its debt.

While shares are down 7% over the last six months, it doesn’t appear to be in any danger, and it’s flourished across a range of environments for more than 50 years, paying its dividend without missing a monthly payment.

In a recent development, as of its latest raise last week, Realty Income pays $3.288 in annualized dividends, up from $3.258. That's a small change of only 0.9%. If it continues like that for the next four quarters, by the end of 2027, it should be $3.408 in annualized dividends. The average of the two is $3.348, and divided by 12, that's an average monthly payment of $0.279.

If you invest $10,000 today at a share price of $57.66 (at the time of writing), that gets you 173 shares, and next year, you'd get about $48.27 every month.

Industry observers note that that may not seem like much, but it's reliable and will continue to rise. It also highlights the need to save for retirement to ensure a livable monthly income.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 6:40PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Intuit ›.

According to recent reports, investors often find themselves choosing between specialized software leaders and broad infrastructure giants. Deciding whether to buy Intuit (INTU -12.77%) or Oracle (ORCL -8.48%) depends on your preference for consumer stability versus enterprise growth.

According to recent reports, intuit serves as the backbone for personal and small business finances, while Oracle provides the essential databases and cloud infrastructure that large organizations require. Both companies are currently integrating artificial intelligence to enhance their platforms. This comparison examines their growth rates, balance sheets, and relative valuations to determine which stock fits best in a 2027 outlook.

Recent findings suggest that intuit provides essential financial technology solutions for millions of global consumers and small businesses through its core brands like TurboTax, QuickBooks, and Credit Karma. The company currently serves approximately 93 million users and relies on major distribution platforms like the Apple (AAPL -1.90%) App Store and Google Play Store. To support its vast software ecosystem, it maintains strategic partnerships with major cloud infrastructure providers including Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) and Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (NASDAQ:GOOG).

In the 12 months ended Oct. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $21.9 billion, representing growth of close to 12.8% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for this time frame was approximately $4.8 billion, reflecting the organization's ability to maintain high net margins while expanding its user base. This steady financial expansion is largely driven by consistent, recurring demand for its digital accounting and tax preparation platforms among mid-market businesses.

Industry observers note that as of its July 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is nearly 0.4x, a metric that compares total debt against the value of shareholder equity to assess financial leverage. The current ratio is approximately 1.5x, reflecting a healthy ability to pay short-term obligations using its most liquid assets. In the fiscal year ended July 31, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $8.7 billion, though note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Oracle offers enterprise software, cloud applications, and infrastructure services through a global delivery model that serves corporations, government agencies, and educational institutions. The manufacturer distributes its complex database systems and cloud applications in more than 145 countries and operates through a network of resellers and system integrators. It recently focused on expanding its presence in tech stocks by building out massive data center capacity specifically designed for high-performance artificial intelligence workloads.

In the 12 months ended Aug. 31, 2026, revenue reached close to $71.8 billion, a significant growth rate of approximately 21.6%. Net income for this period was nearly $18.9 billion, showcasing the scale of its operations as it transitions legacy customers to its newer cloud models. This robust increase in sales is largely attributed to the rapid adoption of its cloud infrastructure services and the ongoing modernization of enterprise data systems.

As of its May 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 3.7x, indicating that the organization uses a substantial amount of debt relative to its equity to fund its capital-intensive operations. The current ratio is roughly 1.1x, suggesting that its ability to meet immediate financial obligations is presently lean compared to more liquid software rivals. In the fiscal year ended May 31, 2026, free cash flow was a negative $23.7 billion because its massive investments in data center equipment and physical assets exceeded the cash generated from day-to-day operations.

Intuit faces intense competition from established rivals and start-ups in the financial software space, particularly those offering lower-cost tax preparation alternatives. The business is heavily dependent on the highly seasonal U.S. tax filing period, which creates significant fluctuations in its annual results and can amplify the impact of any operational delays. It also faces ongoing risks from cybersecurity threats and complex regulatory oversight regarding data privacy and the implementation of artificial intelligence within its consumer products.

Oracle contends with fierce competition in the cloud and software industry from giants like Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) and Amazon. The tech giant deals with a complex supply chain and potential volatility from international operations, including geopolitical instability and trade restrictions that could affect global deployments. Its large-scale transition to a cloud-first strategy requires consistent execution and significant capital spending to avoid losing market share to more specialized infrastructure providers.

With a slightly lower Forward P/E relative to future earnings estimates and a more attractive P/S ratio, Intuit currently trades at a valuation discount relative to Oracle.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

I'd go with Intuit. Small businesses build their books, payroll, and payments around its software, which makes it hard to leave and gives Intuit a dependable base to grow from. And it is now beginning to win larger companies. QuickBooks, TurboTax, and Credit Karma are brands many people already know, and its software for mid-sized businesses is growing about 40% year over year.

What I like is that Intuit keeps returning cash to shareholders, with a dividend that rose 15% over the past year, and it is building AI into its products, so customers can now use QuickBooks inside AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude. Its latest quarter also came in above the company's own targets, and it expects solid growth this year.

In a recent development, to give Oracle its due, it rents out the computing power AI companies need, and its cloud infrastructure sales have more than doubled year over year. But it is borrowing heavily to build data centers and burning cash while it does, and a big share of its contracts comes from one customer, OpenAI.

In a recent development, intuit's growth, by contrast, comes with healthy profits and cash returned to shareholders, not a heavy debt load. For long-term investors, a profitable software company that is expanding into bigger businesses makes Intuit the better buy for 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The resignation of Jensen Huang sent shockwaves through the investment world, with the longtime CEO of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) stepping down following allegations of multiple affairs, including with subordinates and a potential Chinese spy.
  • Let's look at three things that could go right for the semiconductor stock without Huang, and three things that can go wrong.
  • Recent findings suggest that the biggest thing that could go right with Huang gone is that Nvidia's moat remains intact.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:41PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

The resignation of Jensen Huang sent shockwaves through the investment world, with the longtime CEO of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) stepping down following allegations of multiple affairs, including with subordinates and a potential Chinese spy. With its co-founder no longer at its helm, some things will certainly change for the manufacturer.

Let's look at three things that could go right for the semiconductor stock without Huang, and three things that can go wrong.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest thing that could go right with Huang gone is that Nvidia's moat remains intact. The tech giant's moat has long been its CUDA operating system, on which most original artificial intelligence (AI) code was written and optimized for its graphics processing units (GPUs). However, with AI models now showing they can help run models on other chips in just a few days, this moat is promptly shrinking.

In a recent development, CUDA is not Nvidia's only edge, though, and right now it has a large supply chain moat. It has locked down a lot of future supply-constrained high-bandwidth memory (HBM) through a $500 billion deal with SK Hynix (SKHY -13.11%), and it also has the most access to fab capacity at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -9.48%). In a supply-constrained market, availability matters, and right now this is one of Nvidia's biggest advantages.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

Nvidia is growing quickly, and that is expected to continue, with the company recently forecasting that its revenue would climb 75% in fiscal 2028. This growth is being led not just by surging GPU demand, but also by the company getting an ever-increasing piece of the data center revenue pie.

It has been revealed that with its Hopper architecture, Nvidia was capturing about $18 billion in revenue per gigawatt of capacity. Through networking, the addition of more chips like central processing units (CPUs) and language processing units (LPUs), and a more robust software stack, Nvidia is now getting $40 billion per gigawatt for its Vera Rubin System. Keep expanding its system to capture more revenue opportunities, and Nvidia's strong growth will continue.

It has been revealed that trading at a forward P/E of only 9 times fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028) analyst estimates, Nvidia's stock is cheap and has the potential for some substantial multiple expansion. The manufacturer will just have to show that it can continue to grow under newly introduced leadership.

Under Huang, Nvidia developed a close relationship with Elon Musk and SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%), which decided to exclusively build out its data centers on Vera Rubin. SpaceX is set to be one of the most aggressive companies in the space, and if the loss of Huang changes this relationship, it could be a blow to Nvidia's future growth.

Musk has already stated he wants Huang to join his tech giant, and if he does and the company pursues its own chips, it would be a blow to Nvidia.

According to recent reports, even before Huang's departure, there was a push to slow the data center build-out in the U.S., with a large contingent of anti-data-center candidates winning key seats in the midterm elections. This is most likely to impact neoclouds, a major source of revenue for Nvidia.

In a recent development, any delays not only reduce potential sales, but could trigger financing issues for these customers. Neoclouds and enterprise made up 44% of Nvidia's data center revenue in fiscal Q3, so this is no small matter.

Perhaps the biggest risk Nvidia faces with Huang gone is the potential for lost market share and margin compression. Custom AI accelerators and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -13.25%) have been gaining share, and Nvidia's CUDA moat now appears to be dwindling.

In a recent development, if this causes the organization to slash prices to stay competitive, it would significantly reduce its gross margins, potentially putting pressure on earnings even if sales were to continue to grow. This would likely cause the stock to tumble.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

It has been revealed that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to latest inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Sources indicate that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a big reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

If PCE reveals inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

Sources indicate that I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

#85260. College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1382 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1382 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
  • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
  • Sources indicate that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

Sources indicate that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

Merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

Merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

It has been revealed that some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that indicates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

Unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

Some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

Industry observers note that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

Even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

Recent findings suggest that some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

According to recent reports, scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

It has been revealed that which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

It has been revealed that veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

According to recent reports, the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

Think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

Industry observers note that apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Steven Porrello – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:30PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Bloom Energy ›.

Earlier this year, things seemed to be going exactly right for fuel-cell manufacturer Bloom Energy (BE -15.30%).

It's not hard to see why. The race to build AI data centers had stimulated such an enormous appetite for electricity that developers, facing grid bottlenecks and tight construction timelines, simply couldn't afford to wait years for traditional power grid connections.

In that context, upcoming orders for Bloom's fuel-cell systems were coming in hot: First Oracle (ORCL -8.48%) contracted for 1.2 gigawatts (GW) of capacity, then Brookfield Asset Management (BAM -2.53%) expanded its financing framework with Bloom for AI projects from $5 billion to a whopping $25 billion.

Both were significant developments for Bloom's business, and Wall Street absolutely agreed: The stock soared to an all-time high of roughly $350, more than quadrupling in value from where it started the year.

If you take a look at Bloom's stock chart today, however, you'll see a different picture: It has fallen from its high to roughly $168 per share.

That raises the obvious question: What the heck is happening? And, more importantly, should you take this as an occasion to buy Bloom stock?

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

For starters, Bloom is a fuel cell manufacturer. In simple terms, it makes equipment that let data centers and other customers generate electricity on-site rather than waiting years to connect to the grid. These fuel cells are also a source of (relatively) clean power: Instead of burning fuel, they use an electrochemical reaction to convert fuel (such as natural gas) into electricity. It's a pretty neat concept, and it is especially useful for those who need round-the-clock power.

According to recent reports, as mentioned, Bloom stock soared earlier this year as sales of Bloom boxes went through the roof. This hasn't changed. Indeed, third-quarter sales surged 138% year over year to $1.24 billion, prompting management (yet again!) to raise full-year revenue guidance to between $4.4 billion and $4.6 billion. For perspective, its full-year 2025 revenue was about $2 billion.

What has changed, however, is the environment, or more specifically: Wall Street's willingness to pay sky-high valuations for companies associated with the AI boom. Investors have become increasingly concerned about the billions being poured into AI infrastructure, and Bloom, whose future growth is tied to AI spending, has found itself caught in this broader wave of bearish sentiment.

The irony, of course, is that the very numbers that once sent Bloom's stock soaring are no longer enough to reassure investors. But why is that?

If I could capture that shift in perspective in an image, it would be this: Bloom's breathtaking growth this year is like a star's light. It's brilliant to look at, but it tells us more about the past than it does the future. It tells us just how bullish data center developers were on AI infrastructure earlier this year, but it doesn't necessarily indicate how Bloom will fare if that spending slows or stalls.

In other words, Bloom's extraordinary financial results could be a lagging indicator of an AI spending frenzy that is fading, while its stock price reflects anxiety about what will come next.

So, given that Wall Street is concerned about Bloom's future sales, should you reverse course and buy?

Personally, I think this is a great opportunity to pick up Bloom stock. The reaction to concerns over data center construction strikes me as a bit overdone. Even if AI spending slows, the underlying problem Bloom is solving -- an electricity grid struggling to keep up with rising demands -- isn't going away anytime soon. The stock might be volatile today, but for those willing to hold through the volatility, I think today's sell-off offers an attractive opportunity to buy a company with long-term growth potential.

By Katie Brockman – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:30PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

It's been a lucrative year for the stock market, with the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) notching more than two dozen record highs in 2026.

However, the headwinds have been coming in strong lately. Volatility within the tech sector has rattled Wall Street, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) fell into correction territory after plunging nearly 12% from its recent peak, as of this writing.

Recent findings suggest that the bad news for investors is that no bull market can last forever, and it's only a matter of time before we face a pullback. However, Warren Buffett has some timeless advice about how to prepare your portfolio for a potential market crash or recession.

Industry observers note that warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images.

In late 1999, just four months before the dot-com bubble officially popped, Warren Buffett issued a warning to investors in an essay for Fortune. He emphasized that while fresh advancements in technology could transform society, that doesn't necessarily make them smart investments.

Industry observers note that using airlines as an example, Buffett noted that although air travel was revolutionary, 129 airlines had gone bankrupt over the previous 20 years. Televisions and radios fell into the same category as "glamorous businesses that dramatically changed our lives but concurrently failed to deliver rewards to U.S. investors.".

The dot-com bubble eventually proved Buffett's point. While the internet went on to fundamentally transform the world, countless tech stocks crashed and burned in the early 2000s.

"The key to investing is not assessing how much an industry is going to affect society, or how much it will grow," Buffett explained, "but rather determining the competitive advantage of any given company and, above all, the durability of that advantage.".

While it's impossible to say how the market will fare in the coming months, the dot-com bubble serves as a valuable lesson. Artificial intelligence (AI) as a technology could be revolutionary, but that doesn't mean every AI stock will be a good investment. Inevitably, some stocks will flounder during the next downturn.

In a recent development, the best move investors can make now is to load up on a wide variety of quality stocks with robust business fundamentals. While all stocks are vulnerable to short-term volatility, those with strong competitive advantages are the most likely to recover and deliver long-term growth.

According to recent reports, healthy companies will likely thrive over time. Although the S&P 500 lost almost half of its value between 2000 and 2002, the index soared by more than 200% in the two decades following the dot-com bubble.

If we're headed toward a similar bear market, not all stocks will recover. But healthy companies will fuel decades of growth, and the investors who look past the hype and focus on quality stocks will reap the biggest rewards.

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) made history this week with the largest stock market debut on record, securing $81 billion in funding and surpassing SpaceX's initial public offering (IPO) earlier this year.

In a recent development, there was no shortage of investor enthusiasm either, as the stock popped by more than 17% during its first day of trading. While nobody can say how the stock will fare in the coming days or weeks, I predict that some Anthropic investors are about to learn a hard, expensive lesson.

Industry observers note that dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images.

Blockbuster IPOs are often turbulent straight out of the gate, experiencing extreme price swings in their initial weeks and months.

SpaceX, for example, has fallen by more than 20% from its initial price, as of this writing. Semiconductor breakout star SK Hynix has plunged by nearly 30% since it debuted in July, and Meta Platforms – then known as Facebook – sank by more than 50% in its first three months of trading in 2012.

In Meta's case, the stock eventually bounced back, delivering total returns of around 1,400% since its IPO. But the investors who reaped those rewards were those who stayed invested through all the ups and downs rather than expecting immediate riches.

The same thing could be said for Anthropic. Over time, it could be a lucrative investment. The firm recently generated $17 billion in third-quarter revenue, significantly outpacing its $1.4 billion figure from 2025.

But Anthropic also has some major bills to keep up with. Its IPO prospectus disclosed over $900 billion in expense commitments and a $104 billion net operating loss in 2026, and time will tell whether the company's revenue is sufficient to fund the enormous computing power its technology demands.

Industry observers note that this isn't to say that Anthropic is a bad investment. But as with any IPO, there are a lot of unknowns right now, and anything could happen in the coming weeks and months.

If you believe in the business model and are willing to hold your investment for at least a few years despite any potential short-term volatility, it could be a smart buy – assuming it's part of a well-diversified portfolio.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that however, investors who are buying primarily because of the hype around the stock, hoping to make a quick buck, have the most to lose. The short term is likely to be a bumpy ride, and those who are only buying with the hope of earning a fortune overnight could end up sorely disappointed.

Fundamentals beat hype every time, and the strongest investments are those with solid underlying business fundamentals and long-term growth potential.

  • Recent findings suggest that one of the biggest investment opportunities in the market right now is in memory chip stocks, with Micron (MU -13.89%) and Sandisk (SNDK -16.05%) being the two best options.
  • There are many unknowns surrounding Nvidia right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:03PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Micron Technology ›.

It has been revealed that nvidia has grabbed all the headlines in recent weeks, mainly over what's going on with former CEO Jensen Huang. This has pummeled the stock, but there are other stocks benefiting from the same tailwinds as Nvidia that don't have the same headline risk right now.

Recent findings suggest that one of the biggest investment opportunities in the market right now is in memory chip stocks, with Micron (MU -13.89%) and Sandisk (SNDK -16.05%) being the two best options. But are they better than Nvidia? Let's take a look.

There are many unknowns surrounding Nvidia right now. Whether it's questions about how much of its chip sales may be going to China through third parties, or whether all of the demand was legitimate, nobody knows. However, one point that's not up for debate is that demand for AI computing is real, and it has stretched memory chip suppliers to their limits.

It has been revealed that both Micron and Sandisk have sold out of production capacity, and it could be that way for many years, despite both companies opening new facilities in the near future to raise capacity. Micron's management team told investors that it expects memory chip market conditions to be worse in 2027 and 2028 than in 2026, an incredible statement, given how bad things are right now. This will keep memory chip prices elevated for some time, which is fantastic news for investors.

Both have a long history of being highly cyclical companies, with good times when demand is high and downturns when there is excess supply. Historically, these cycles don't last for much more than a year, and that's exactly what the market is expecting this time around.

However, with AI hyperscalers needing much more computing capacity, this build-out could last until 2030 or beyond.

That's a lot of time for both Sandisk and Micron to produce a ton of profits and reshape their futures, while also delivering huge investor returns on the way.

They are doing this by reshaping their business models. Sandisk and Micron are starting to sign long-term agreements with their clients, which sets a floor and a ceiling on memory prices. While this cuts out some of the peaks, it prevents these two from going into deep downturns when demand isn't as high. That sets their businesses up for long-term success.

But can their returns trump Nvidia?

Because the market is expecting a cyclical downturn any day now, each of these stocks is valued at a dirt cheap level.

MU PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

According to recent reports, with both stocks at about 4 times this year's projected earnings (both companies are already in fiscal year 2027), that's a huge discount to the broader market. Nvidia is also cheap at about 10 times next year's earnings, but that pales in comparison to these two.

This makes these two excellent options, but only if the market comes around to valuing them properly. If the market keeps these two at low valuations due to concerns about their cyclical nature, these stocks may be duds. However, I don't see that happening.

Industry observers note that both Sandisk and Micron have been repurchasing shares with their profits, which allows them to artificially boost earnings per share by decreasing the number of shares outstanding. This is nothing new and has been done successfully by many companies in the market.

With their share prices low relative to their profits, each dollar spent on buybacks is more effective. This could deliver strong long-term returns and lead to outperformance of Nvidia.

Although I think Nvidia will be OK over the long term, these two memory chip stocks may be a safer bet. Investors may want to see who the next CEO of Nvidia is before jumping back into the stock, and these two make for great alternatives with huge upside.
