Latest Update: Legendary commentator CLIVE TYLDESLEY on how his ITV exit has made hearts grow fonder, the rise of YouTube streamers, his lockdown money-spinner - and why he refuses to be another loud voice in the game

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1678 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Clive Tyldesley reaches for his glasses as he rummages through the commentary charts crammed into an old filing cabinet, jokes about his fading eyesight and supposes one day he will no longer be able to identify footballers from the gantry.
  • Fortunately, we are still far from that point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 15 November 2026.

Clive Tyldesley reaches for his glasses as he rummages through the commentary charts crammed into an old filing cabinet, jokes about his fading eyesight and supposes one day he will no longer be able to identify footballers from the gantry.

Fortunately, we are still far from that point. At 72, Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever. His eyes are perfectly good when bespectacled, his mind nimble enough to keep up with play and his soothingly familiar voice strong and authoritative with a gentle tendency towards self-deprecation.

This much was evident as Manchester United roared back to beat Roma in the Champions League and a clip of his spine-tingling commentary from the live CBS broadcast circulated on social media and found an appreciative audience in Europe.

'I don't know if there's an element of nostalgia in hearing my voice again,' notes Tyldesley. 'If I'm honest, I've dodged the worst of the public's ire with everything including commentators because I haven't been around for the last few years.

Sources indicate that 'Absence has made a few hearts grow a little fonder towards me and maybe if I'd been on Sky every week for the last six years, I'd be no less unpopular than anybody else out there. So, I can't pretend it's not nice to get some engagement with an audience I used to commentate to on a regular basis, but I'm very happy where I am.'.

Tyldesley has been the lead commentator for the CBS coverage of the Champions League since 2020, converting transfer fees into US dollars and keeping his measurements imperial for a North American audience but otherwise approaching the job as he always did.

Clive Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever at 72 and is 'very happy' in his role as the lead commentator of CBS coverage of the Champions League.

Tyldesley's commentary of Man United's comeback against Roma circulated on social media and received an appreciative audience in Europe.

The 72-year-old wonders whether there was an element of nostalgia to the reaction, with Tyldesley's work for CBS meaning his commentary cannot be shown in Europe.

Clips of the studio panel featuring Thierry Henry, Micah Richards, Jamie Carragher and presenter Kate Scott are popular on social media but live action featuring Tyldesley's commentary is governed by broadcasting rights deals and cannot be shown in Europe.

The one from Old Trafford of Matheus Cunha's winning goal in the 86th minute slipped through the net on X and reminded everyone his passion for football is undimmed, and his voice can still stand hairs on attention.

Recent findings suggest that 'I don't think I've seen a better game than the first leg of the Paris Saint-Germain v Bayern Munich Champions League semi-final,' indicates Tyldesley on the rare quality of Europe's elite competition. 'I listened to people with hundreds more England caps than me saying it was bad defending, but I watched the whole game back the next day and it wasn't.

Industry observers note that 'I'm sorry but it was wonderful attacking and a show of intent by two coaches who trusted defenders to defend one-on-one and attackers to score more than the opposition. Rob Green was my co-commentator and at the end we just put our microphones down and looked at each other and noted, "Wow.".

Industry observers note that 'I've not forgotten muddy pitches and assassin centre backs. You only need to look on YouTube to see football was different, but you can't pretend it was better. I see terrible games today just as I did then, but particularly in the Champions League, I regularly stumble upon football that gets me off my seat.'.

His exit from ITV, first displaced by Sam Matterface as lead commentator in 2020 and then released entirely after Euro 2024 clearly smarted but Tyldesley is comfortable as the veteran in the fast-changing media landscape.

'Most of the principles I picked up from watching John Motson, Barry Davies and Brian Moore in their pomp are applicable to commentary in 2026,' he says. 'There's no need to reinvent that particular wheel.

According to recent reports, 'You can offer alternatives such as fan zones and screaming watchalongs for people to view it in a different way. I make it my business to look at J_Tekkz or LDN Movements or whatever is pulling in millions on YouTube.

Tyldesley believes he has not seen a better game than the first leg of PSG's Champions League semi-final with Bayern Munich last year.

The veteran commentator believes most of the principles he learned starting out still apply, but admits to having watched popular newly introduced voices to see if anything could apply to his commentary.

Tyldesley also works as a guest lecturer and commentates for blockbuster computer games, as well as selling framed prints of his commentary charts.

'I sample a bit of Mark Goldbridge to see why he's prominent but I'm hearing nothing in those guys applicable to the way I call a football match so I carry on with the same focus I've always had on what constitutes good commentary.'.

The central principle being that the game is bigger than the individuals in it, he points out, with viewers tuning in for the football not the commentator.

'The biggest challenge for a television commentator is to find the right words at the major moments, to go beyond "amazing," "brilliant", "incredible" and try to add some editorial context,' says Tyldesley.

'Every goal is unique. The words following a goal that is going to be remembered for years should be unique and specific to that goal, but that's difficult to do. It's unscripted performance and difficult to master and capture.

'I am concentrating hardest for the 10-15 seconds after a massive goal because I'm searching for words which will become a small part of people's memories. That's very different to consciously trying to provide 45-second soundbites to amplify one's own personality and standing on social media.

'There's a danger of media leaning that way as it develops such an emphasis on the bitesize.'.

Among other things, Tyldesley is a guest lecturer for media students at the University of Salford, still doing commentaries for blockbuster computer games and selling framed prints of his commentary charts, something that started as 'a silly idea in lockdown'.

Recent findings suggest that his wife Susan bought a dozen frames to see how it went. Originally, he offered three Champions League finals won by English clubs in 1999, 2005 and 2012. He sent one each to Gary Neville who played for Manchester United in 1999 and Jamie Carragher who played for Liverpool in 2005. They both posted images online and demand skyrocketed.

In a recent development, 'Two good friends,' smiles Tyldesley. 'I probably got about half a million pounds of free advertising out of them.' Sales have soared beyond 50,000. There's a Celtic chart on the gym in Rod Stewart's house. Ant and Dec have bought signed Newcastle charts.

His own venture into podcasting was short-lived and he politely declines between five and ten invitations each week to appear on others.

'I've tried to step back from that kind of thing,' notes Tyldesley. 'So much content I hear on football is empty, verbose and repetitive. Really, there are only so many things you can say about Alexander Isak having his shirt pulled in mid-air and Gary Neville probably remarked most of them in the 30 seconds following the incident.

Tyldesley has no intends to retire and Paramount, the owners of his employers CBS - and soon to be the owners of TNT Sports - will have the UK rights for the Champions League.

Sales of his framed commentary charts, something that started during lockdown, have soared beyond 50,000.

It has been revealed that 'There are so many brutally judgmental loud voices in and around football attracting attention that I want to be as far away from as possible, so that's what I do. Unless I sense an opportunity to talk about communication and broadcasting rather than whether club A, B or C should replace their manager. That's not for me Clive.'.

Industry observers note that so, there's a little less Tyldesley out there than there was. He was content to stay at home and watch the World Cup from his sofa this summer for the first time since 1990.

But there are no intends to retire. And who knows what might change next season when Paramount, the owners of CBS – and soon to be the owners of current rights holders TNT Sports – have the UK rights for the Champions League.

There might be a familiar voice beamed into our living rooms once again.

When I saw the Dear England play, I was the only person in the theatre who didn't enjoy it, and that was because I hated the portrayal of Harry Kane.

He was written as an uneducated numbskull. Written to laugh at and the theatre laughed at him. He was stupid and gullible, another thick footballer.

And anyone who has spent time with footballers will know they might lack for an Eton College education but are streetwise and invariably smart with a razor sharp sense of humour.

Kane is a leader of those men. There's not a single thing about the person Kane has made himself to laugh or sneer at and I wanted to stand up in the theatre that afternoon and shout at everyone.

Oddly, I was introduced to the playwright James Graham at a function a few weeks later and he kind of pushed me for my opinion of Dear England.

I tried to be diplomatic, but I felt so strongly I ended up scolding him for writing a character called Harry Kane who was nothing like Harry Kane.

It has been revealed that so, that was the end of a beautiful friendship before it began. And I'm so thrilled now there's a better appreciation of the person Harry is.

By Dominic Basulto – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:30PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Securitize ›.

If you only look at a stock chart for Securitize (SECZ -7.45%), you might miss the bigger picture.

Yes, Securitize is down 47% since it went public in July. But there's a fast-expanding financial trend that could significantly move the dial for Securitize in the years ahead: real-world asset tokenization.

Asset tokenization is taking off by leaps and bounds. The value of the tokenized equities market is now $3.8 billion, and Securitize is one of the key reasons why. The manufacturer is at the forefront of asset tokenization, the process of transforming real-world assets (such as stocks and bonds) into digital assets that reside on the blockchain.

Sources indicate that by all accounts, asset tokenization could be a multitrillion-dollar market opportunity. There are simply too many cost savings and efficiency gains to be had from tokenization. And U.S. regulators, using a newly introduced "innovation exemption," have now cleared the way for tokenized equities to begin trading on exchanges and blockchain trading platforms.

  • Sources indicate that every time it looks like the S&P 500 is starting to drop, investors send it back up.
  • Sources indicate that however, there's bound to be a crash at some point, whether before the year's out or into the future.
  • Shopify is a top e-commerce firm that provides services to e-commerce retailers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jennifer Saibil – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:33PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Shopify ›.

Sources indicate that every time it looks like the S&P 500 is starting to drop, investors send it back up. As of this writing, it's no longer a double-digit increase year to date, but it's still up an admirable 7%. That's cautious optimism considering high inflation and rising interest rates.

Sources indicate that however, there's bound to be a crash at some point, whether before the year's out or into the future. Whenever it happens, I would buy Shopify (SHOP -6.25%), Costco Wholesale (COST +0.76%), and e.l.f. Beauty (ELF -5.01%) stocks, all of which are great businesses but have rich price tags.

Shopify is a top e-commerce firm that provides services to e-commerce retailers. Its products range from total, all-inclusive websites to single products like payment systems or cross-border e-commerce, and it has moved from helping small businesses thrive to working with enterprise retailers like Estee Lauder's (EL -2.27%) Clinique and Lululemon Athletica (LULU -2.76%). That's because it takes away the pain points of companies having to develop these kinds of systems themselves, and it has developed a reputation for its services that make it their partner of choice.

Even though it started as an e-commerce company, offering an easy path for small retailers to get online, it now calls itself simply a commerce company. It works with omnichannel retailers, unifying all of a company's brick-and-mortar and digital channels into one management system. The company describes its evolution as "However commerce evolves, Shopify will be the engine behind it. The merchants who are the backbone of the economy demand it of us.".

Recent findings suggest that despite inflation and lots of competition, Shopify's revenue is accelerating, up 32% year over year in the third quarter, and its gross merchandise volume (GMV), or the volume of sales on its platform from its clients, increased 29%. At $119 billion, it was higher than Amazon's (AMZN -4.10%) online and third-party sales of $116 billion. Amazon and Shopify have a partnership, too, whereby shoppers can use Amazon's Buy With Prime as a checkout through participating Shopify retailers.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

What's been stopping me from buying so far is the expensive price tag. At the current price, Shopify stock trades at 75 times trailing 12-month earnings, making it the most expensive stock on this list. That speaks to investor confidence, but it also builds in a lot of growth.

Costco has a unique retail model that has proven to work through any kind of economic backdrop. It offers rock-bottom prices, but shoppers have to pay an annual fee to shop there. Considering its high renewal rates, consistently increasing membership metrics, and the number of members who upgrade to the executive membership, which costs double the standard rate, shoppers find the deal worthwhile.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, as inflation rises and customers become more cautious about spending, Costco’s sales growth has accelerated. In the 2026 fiscal fourth quarter (ended Aug. 30), sales increased 11.2% year over year, driven by a 9.4% increase in comparable sales. Some of that came from the company's gas stations as oil prices increased, and that's become an important growth driver. It's also highly profitable, and earnings per share (EPS) increased from $5.87 to $6.75.

It has been revealed that but it gets better. Costco also reports monthly metrics, and sales increased 13% in both September and October. On top of that, Costco just announced a $30 special dividend. Costco's regular dividend only yields 0.53%, but it pays a special dividend on average every two and a half years. Adding $30 to this year's payout would bring the effective yield to 3.2%.

Recent findings suggest that however, Costco stock trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 53, which is a major premium to other retailers. The market obviously thinks it's worth it, but the stock is priced for perfection.

E.l.f. has carved out a niche in mass cosmetics as an eco-friendly brand with luxury dupes. It has become one of the largest companies of its kind, breaking into an industry dominated by legacy brands from which it’s pulling market share. It's also a newcomer in the luxury cosmetics industry, with its recent acquisition of Hailey Bieber's Rhode brand.

In the 2027 fiscal Q2 (ended Sept. 30), sales increased 51% year over year, and gross margin increased 1.7 percentage points to 71%. E.l.f. stock has plunged after tariffs were introduced last year, but tariff refunds have improved its gross margin, and the stock has nearly doubled since it bottomed out last June.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that it's the most popular cosmetics manufacturer in the Piper Sandler (PIPR -4.03%) Taking Stock With Teens Survey, and Rhode is the third. It's now also the top or second-largest brand in 22 cosmetics categories, up from 11 in 2021.

It has been revealed that E.l.f. stock trades at 72 times trailing 12-month earnings, and if a broader market sell-off knocks that multiple closer to 40 or 45, I'd be ready to buy the stock—alongside Shopify and Costco.

Intel Claims It Just Signed Its First Customer for Its Most Advanced Chipmaking Process. The Stock Is Still More Than 60% Below Its June Record.

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (867 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Intel (INTC -7.97%) CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday, Nov.
  • Intel's tech chief, Pushkar Ranade, later clarified on X that it had signed up for 18A-P, an upgraded version of 18A, the company's most advanced manufacturing process.
  • Sources indicate that for a organization still working to build a manufacturing business for other chip designers, the signing is a milestone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:47PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Intel ›.

Recent findings suggest that "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Intel (INTC -7.97%) CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas.

He didn't name the customer. Intel's tech chief, Pushkar Ranade, later clarified on X that it had signed up for 18A-P, an upgraded version of 18A, the company's most advanced manufacturing process. CNBC, which reported Tan's remarks, called it the first outside customer for Intel's 18A chips.

Sources indicate that for a organization still working to build a manufacturing business for other chip designers, the signing is a milestone. Shares haven't gotten a lift from it, though. Intel stock closed at around $55 on Tuesday, Nov. 17, and closed near $51 on Friday, Nov. 20 -- more than 60% below its record close of $140.94 on June 22.

I think that response makes sense. A signed customer starts a foundry relationship, but it isn't revenue yet. And Intel's own numbers show how small its outside manufacturing business still is.

Intel might never tell investors who the customer is.

According to recent reports, "As is standard practice in the foundry business, I have consistently maintained that we will not disclose customer details," Tan said in prepared remarks for Intel's Oct. 29 earnings call.

Recent findings suggest that A name could still come from the customer's side. That same Wednesday, Intel remarked Microsoft is the first firm to announce use of its EMIB chip packaging tech, for chips Microsoft designs for its Azure cloud.

Sure, outside companies have lined up behind Intel's latest technology before. Microsoft mentioned in February 2024 that it planned to produce a chip design on Intel 18A. That September, Intel said it would build an artificial intelligence (AI) networking chip for Amazon's Amazon Web Services on 18A too. And in August, Japanese chip designer Socionext (OTC:SOCNF) said it would use 18A-P to develop custom chips.

It has been revealed that still, Tan described this customer as signed, and Ranade linked it to 18A-P, so it's arguably the first customer signed for that process. Investors still don't know how many chips the customer plans to buy and when Intel gets paid.

According to recent reports, intel's third-quarter foundry revenue grew 58% year over year to $6.7 billion, but most of it came from Intel's own product groups. Revenue from outside customers was $411 million, compared to $293 million in the second quarter and just $32 million a year before. Intel noted the third-quarter jump came mostly from a non-recurring customer program. And in its quarterly filing, the company said substantially all of its foundry business still supports manufacturing for Intel's own products.

So, outside revenue is growing, but it's still around 6% of Intel's foundry sales, and the latest quarter relied on a one-time contract.

The losses are shrinking, at least. The foundry's third-quarter operating loss was $1.9 billion, around $240 million less than in the second quarter and almost $470 million less than a year before.

"These results represent meaningful progress, although we still have considerable work ahead of us to deliver a sustainably profitable Foundry business," CFO David Zinsner noted in Intel's prepared remarks for the Oct. 29 call.

For the signing to matter to shareholders, I think the customer would have to come forward, since Intel won't name it. Intel's 18A-P process also has to move from risk production, which began in June, to volume.

It has been revealed that intel says the process is on track to launch across its own products by year-end, but it hasn't stated when an outside customer's chips will follow. The deal also needs to show up as recurring outside revenue instead of another one-time program.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

More is at stake, too. Intel said in its last quarterly filing that committed demand for 14A, its next process, will dictate how fast and how far it expands manufacturing. That includes demand from potential significant outside customers. A signed 18A-P customer could help Intel get those commitments. But a deal on 18A-P isn't a commitment to 14A.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, investors are already paying plenty for Intel's future profits. At around $51, the stock trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of about 29 on next year's expected earnings. And Intel expects non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share to fall to $0.25 in the fourth quarter from $0.52 in the third.

Recent findings suggest that tan's announcement is progress for a foundry that's mainly made Intel's own chips. But until the customer is named and its chips show up in Intel's outside revenue, I don't think it changes much for the stock.

  • Nine months ago, United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered an anomaly with one of its Vulcan Centaur rockets, forcing it to pause operations while it worked out a fix.
  • A successful launch would advance Amazon's effort to build a satellite communications system to rival SpaceX's Starlink.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Rich Smith – Nov 21, 2026 at 9:27PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Amazon ›.

A crisis was forming in the space industry.

It has been revealed that for months, Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) CEO Elon Musk had been making noises about ending commercial rolls out of its Falcon 9 rocket -- the rocket that, in 2025, debuted more than 80% of all payloads to orbit worldwide. At the time, rockets from rival companies Arianespace, Blue Origin, and United Launch Alliance were all grounded for a variety of technical glitches.

Nine months ago, United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered an anomaly with one of its Vulcan Centaur rockets, forcing it to pause operations while it worked out a fix. But at long last, ULA was ready to return to flight. In a mission slated for Nov. 15, Vulcan would return to flight, carrying a payload of 40 Leo communications satellites into orbit for customer Amazon (AMZN -4.10%).

A successful launch would advance Amazon's effort to build a satellite communications system to rival SpaceX's Starlink. At the same time, it would alleviate the concerns of space companies worried that Falcon 9's retirement would deprive them of access to space. With ULA back in the race, there'd once again be an alternative to SpaceX.

That's what a successful launch would have meant -- but it's not what actually happened.

Instead, for the first time in its history as a space manufacturer, ULA suffered a total mission failure -- all cargo lost. As ULA explained, its Vulcan rocket "lost telemetry and the mission at approximately 10 minutes into flight," although the real problem occurred before that.

Vulcan Centaur includes two stages: BE-4 engines from Blue Origin power the Vulcan first stage, supplemented by RL10 side boosters from L3Harris(LHX -2.59%). In flight, the RL10s are first to drop off the rocket, followed by the entire first stage detaching approximately six minutes into flight. Then the Centaur second stage takes over and lifts the payload the rest of the way into orbit.

After several days of examining the data, ULA now believes the RL10 boosters and the second-stage Centaur both performed nominally. The problem must therefore lie with the Vulcan first stage -- specifically, preliminary indications as of Wednesday suggest Vulcan's fuel supply to the BE-4 engines, rather than the engines themselves, was the culprit. This first stage performed poorly in the boost stage, failing to accelerate the vehicle sufficiently for the Centaur to lift the payload all the way into orbit.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

For Amazon, either culprit would be bad news.

Aiming to accelerate its deployment of Leo satellites so that it can begin competing with SpaceX in satellite internet, Amazon splashed out billions of dollars to reserve launches on 38 Vulcan Centaur rockets, 18 Arianespace Ariane 6es, and anywhere from 12 to 27 Blue Origin New Glenns.

It's also reserved launches on some of ULA's older Atlas V rockets. So far, those have done most of the work of putting nearly 400 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit (with significant help from SpaceX's Falcon 9, which Amazon reluctantly added to the lineup in 2023). The problem is, ULA is just about out of Atlas V rockets (and isn't building more). And SpaceX Falcon 9 launches are all booked up through 2028 (and SpaceX also doesn't plan to add more).

In a recent development, this leaves Amazon largely dependent on ULA's Vulcan Centaur -- which just proved itself unreliable. And this problem may get even bigger; after all, the same BE-4 engine that appears to be at the root of Vulcan's problems also powers Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket. And that could put New Glenn on the sidelines as well.

(Or it may not. While the investigation is still at an early stage, as of Wednesday, ULA believes "preliminary indications" suggest Vulcan's fuel supply to the BE-4 engines, and not the engines themselves, is the culprit. If that's the case, then Blue Origin's New Glenn may not be affected.).

Still, until this is all resolved, it appears that Amazon currently has no reliable means of putting Leo satellites into orbit.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that in the meantime, SpaceX Starlink, already the leader in satellite internet, is likely to remain so for the foreseeable future. More than that: the longer Amazon is forced to cool its heels down here on Earth, the wider the gap between SpaceX and [insert name of literally anyone else who might want to compete with SpaceX].

Amazon's pain, I fear, is going to be SpaceX's gain.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's strategy to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

Recent findings suggest that the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's strategy to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

Recent findings suggest that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

In a recent development, dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

The U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio said. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

Bessent stated in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

After years of overspending, Dalio noted total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

To solve this, Dalio mentioned the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

First, Dalio said the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Fresh York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

"All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio stated. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that dalio stated it's crucial to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

According to recent reports, dalio mentioned the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder said.

Sources indicate that dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.
    • According to recent reports, david Tepper of Appaloosa Management is considered one of the world's top hedge fund managers, and through his investment prowess, he's amassed an estimated net worth of $28.5 billion.
    • Industry observers note that while Tepper's track record speaks for itself, I think he got it wrong in this case.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 21, 2026 at 10:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

    According to recent reports, david Tepper of Appaloosa Management is considered one of the world's top hedge fund managers, and through his investment prowess, he's amassed an estimated net worth of $28.5 billion. The Carolina Panthers' owner was reshuffling his artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor positions in Q3, exiting positions in Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -13.25%) and Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%), while buying shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) and Micron (MU -13.89%). He also cut his stake in Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) nearly in half.

    Industry observers note that while Tepper's track record speaks for itself, I think he got it wrong in this case. Here's why.

    In a recent development, while Tepper was buying Nvidia shares before Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO, the company is facing potential concerns beyond the loss of its CEO. Competitors have started to catch up, with Semianalysis recently reporting that Alphabet's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), which it co-developed with Broadcom, are delivering better performance per dollar. Meanwhile, all of Nvidia's largest customers, outside of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) are working on developing their own custom chips.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The AI application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) market is growing much more swiftly than the GPU market, with Counterpoint Research projecting that custom AI chip unit shipments will surpass data center GPU shipments in 2028. Two of the biggest winners from this trend are Alphabet and Broadcom.

    Sources indicate that alphabet developed its TPUs more than a decade ago, and its comprehensive ecosystem is starting to rival Nvidia's. Not only is TPU growth supported by Alphabet's internal use and its cloud offering, but it is also beginning to sell its solutions to external data center operators, such as Anthropic and OpenAI.

    It has been revealed that bloomberg Intelligence believes that TPU sales outside of Google Cloud could grow from just $12 billion this year to over $135 billion in 2028. This is a huge revenue driver for both Alphabet and Broadcom, which appear to be two of the biggest winners in this rotation.

    In a recent development, even bigger news for Nvidia competitors, though, is that Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) revealed that its Claude Mythos model demonstrated that it can get models up to speed running on AMD GPUs in just two to three days without any human involvement, dramatically cutting down the six to 12 months it used to take a dozen engineers to get models running on different chips. This greatly narrows Nvidia's CUDA moat and opens the door for both AMD and ASICs to take market share.

    The timing is great for AMD, as it recently started shipping its complete Helios systems, which combine its GPUs, CPUs, and networking into one package, to large hyperscaler customers. It's significantly cheaper than Nvidia's end-to-end server racks, opening the door to take more market share if it can show strong performance. The firm's CPUs will also play a key role in Alphabet's latest TPU 8tx AI system.

    With CUDA's moat weakening, Alphabet, Broadcom, and AMD, all of which have cheaper offerings, should benefit greatly in the coming years. Meanwhile, Nvidia could face not just a loss of share but also margin compression. This could lead to lower profitability even if it can grow its revenue. That's one of the massive reasons I prefer the three stocks Tepper was selling over Nvidia.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    As for the other semiconductor stock that Tepper was buying, Micron, I'd be careful. Memory has historically experienced very massive boom-and-bust cycles, and, while this supercycle is certainly different, memory still tends to be a commodity.

    Micron is also the most exposed of the major dynamic random access memory (DRAM) makers to any changes in prices of conventional memory, with it having the smallest share of the high bandwidth memory (HBM) market, which has been the driving force of the industry.

    Another area of worry is with NAND, or flash memory. While Micron derives the bulk of its memory from DRAM, NAND has grown to about a quarter of its revenue. Hong Kong-based GF Securities recently issued a note saying it expects this market to become oversupplied as soon as next year. While primarily a DRAM maker, Micron would not be immune to a massive price pullback in the NAND market.

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 10:10PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Caterpillar ›.

    Wall Street gets excited about stock splits, with some investors attempting to get ahead of a split before it is declared. Caterpillar (CAT -5.01%), Comfort Systems (FIX -6.42%), and GE Vernova (GEV -7.53%) are all candidates for a stock split, with share prices that are, in some cases, well above $500. Even after the pullback in the artificial intelligence trade, each of these stocks remains a strong candidate for a stock split. Based on its price, Comfort Systems could be the first to do so. Here's what you need to know.

    Industry observers note that from a purely functional point of view, a stock split makes a firm's stock cheaper. For example, as of this writing, Comfort Systems' stock price was roughly $1,100 per share (rounding down). A two-for-one split would lower that to around $550 per share; a 10-for-1 split would bring the price down to $110. It is clearly easier for an investor to afford to buy a single share of a $110 stock than it is to buy a single share of a $1,100 stock. That's as true on the financial side as it is one the emotional side, since buying a single share may not feel worth the effort while buying 10 feels like a more substantial investment, even if both investments would end up costing $1,100.

    Sources indicate that from a financial perspective, however, a stock split has very little meaning. All that is being done is that a single share is now split into two or some other number of shares. To keep the math simple, if a company had just one share, it would represent 100% ownership. A two-for-one split would simply mean that there were two shares, each representing 50% ownership. A 10-for-1 split would mean there were 10 shares, each representing 10% ownership. If you owned the original share, representing 100% ownership, you would own more shares and still have 100% ownership after a stock split. Nothing changed about the percentage of the company you own.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, per-share figures such as earnings per share are adjusted, but the base number remains the same. For example, if a company with one share earned $10, earnings per share would be $10. After a 10-for-1 split, the company's earnings per share would be $1, but its earnings would still be $10. Again, nothing material changed about the company.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In other words, a stock split isn't a particularly big deal. But investors often view such events as vital and bid up the shares of companies that split their stocks. That remains true even as more brokers allow fractional purchases, which means you can invest a dollar amount rather than buy based on the number of whole shares you can afford.

    Recent findings suggest that right now, the stock prices of each of these companies are falling. That reduces the likelihood of a cut, with GE Vernova and Comfort Systems both off their 52-week highs by nearly 50%, and Caterpillar down roughly 35% from its high. Stock splits often happen on the way up; they are less likely on the way down. The pullback is due to investors being less enthusiastic about the artificial intelligence (AI) trade than earlier in the year.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Caterpillar makes construction equipment for building AI data centers and the power systems that supply them. GE Vernova makes turbines that generate the energy AI needs to operate, with demand coming from utilities and, increasingly, directly from data center operators looking to generate their own power. And Comfort Systems is a building and service provider that works on mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, all of which are important for building an AI data center.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    All three of these industrial companies have huge backlogs and will likely benefit from AI spending for years to come. That noted, Comfort Systems has the highest stock price here, at a bit over $1,100. Cat is next at around $750, with GE Vernova at a bit over $530. And that's after the large drawdowns noted above. Given this information, Comfort Systems seems like the most likely candidate for a stock split.

    At the end of the day, stock splits are more of an emotional phenomenon than a financial one. You probably shouldn't buy a stock just because you think it may split. You should buy it because you like the tech giant enough to own it, preferably for the long term.

    By Todd Shriber – Nov 21, 2026 at 10:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Energy ETF ›.

    Recent findings suggest that elections have a way of eliciting emotional, borderline-visceral reactions in the investment community. Still, the knee-jerk responses are often confined to the immediate aftermath and, over time, cooler heads ultimately prevail.

    For those in the camp of doing nothing with their portfolios following the blue wave, there's nothing wrong with that line of thinking. That's a calm, rational approach, and one that is validated by history.

    Industry observers note that since 1950, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) has been positive in the year following every midterm election, with an average gain of 15% over those 12 months. So if history holds up, now isn't the time to sell stocks.

    In a recent development, investors don’t need to do a lot post-election portfolio tinkering, but these ETFs may be worth examining. Image source: Getty Images.

    Sources indicate that on the other hand, changes in congressional majorities may usher in opportunities for tactical investors to capitalize on the new legislative landscape. Likewise (and perhaps surprisingly), some sectors and industries previously considered vulnerable to the Democratic sweep may prove to be less so. With that in mind, here are some exchange-traded funds (ETFs) I'm spying following the election.

    It's not surprising that the healthcare sector is in the spotlight following Election Day, but this is an example of investors needing to be tactical. Noted another way, a standard pharmaceutical-heavy ETF may not be the best way to capitalize on the shift of power in Congress. That's why I'm evaluating the iShares U.S. Healthcare Providers ETF (IHF +0.74%).

    Recent findings suggest that this $1.6 billion ETF, which turned 20 years old in May, holds shares of health insurance providers and service operators. Those could be some of the best healthcare stocks to own at a time when Democrats could push to restore, even in part, the Affordable Care Act's enhanced premium subsidies that fell by the wayside at the end of 2025. There's also chatter about momentum to add long-term care coverage to Medicare, which could benefit some of this ETF's 61 holdings.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that the new congressional majority could also scrap or significantly limit planned cuts to Medicaid. If Democrats are successful in leveraging government funding to increase insurance coverage, some of this ETF's holdings will benefit from higher enrollment and reduced exposure to uncompensated care.

    Be advised that this ETF is top-heavy, as UnitedHealth and CVS Health combine for nearly a third of its portfolio.

    It has been revealed that the Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE -0.73%) and the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT -7.00%) are both examples of sector ETFs that were decked following Election Day. Since Nov. 4, the first trading day after Election Day, the energy fund dipped 5.3% while its tech counterpart slumped 15.3%.

    Sources indicate that the reasons differ. As has been widely noted, data center stocks are retreating not only because Democrats will control Congress but also because the party holds 30 of 50 governors' mansions, including some in states where data centers were front and center on Election Day.

    In a recent development, clearly, rhetoric opposed to data centers is effective on the campaign trail. Still, the Vanguard tech ETF may not be worth dumping today because it's hard to get data center moratoriums across the legislative finish line. Before Election Day, only Upcoming York state was successful in climbing that mountain.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that as for the Vanguard Energy ETF, its post-election weakness isn't surprising. Renewable energy stocks often rally when polls and election results favor Democrats while the fossil fuel names that dominate this Vanguard ETF languish. That scenario played out this year.

    Don't rush to abandon or ignore this Vanguard fund. The reasoning is simple: The energy sector has noteworthy short-term earnings momentum, and the group is proving to be an effective portfolio hedge while high interest rates diminish the diversification benefits of bonds.

    On that note, it should be acknowledged that energy stocks have been negatively correlated with the broader market for much of this year, implying that the Vanguard Energy ETF can enhance a portfolio’s diversification.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that netflix's (NFLX -2.96%) share price has been cut in half from the all-time high it reached last summer.
    • While there are reasons for the huge drop in Netflix, including slowing revenue growth and concerns about engagement, the drop prompted billionaire investor Bill Ackman to add the stock back to Pershing Square's (PS -8.77%) portfolio earlier this year.
    • To be sure, Netflix's revenue growth has slowed considerably this year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Levy – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

    Recent findings suggest that netflix's (NFLX -2.96%) share price has been cut in half from the all-time high it reached last summer. The stock now trades below $60 per share, as of this writing.

    While there are reasons for the huge drop in Netflix, including slowing revenue growth and concerns about engagement, the drop prompted billionaire investor Bill Ackman to add the stock back to Pershing Square's (PS -8.77%) portfolio earlier this year. The stock has continued to drop, though, but Ackman doesn't see that as a concern. In fact, he sees it as an incredible opportunity for investors.

    To be sure, Netflix's revenue growth has slowed considerably this year. Revenue grew between 15.9% and 17.6% in the four quarters through the first quarter of this year. That rate slowed to 13.4% in the second quarter and 11.8% in the third quarter. Management forecasts just 11.5% growth in the fourth quarter.

    Management wasn't afraid to touch on the reasons for the slowdown. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos remarked the U.S. is "just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we'd like," during the manufacturer's third-quarter earnings call. The advertising business has also been weaker than expected. "We are at the moment a bit behind our aggressive target for the year," Co-CEO Greg Peters said on the call. And that stems from disappointing engagement. "We want to grow view hours faster. We're not satisfied. We're working on it," CFO Spencer Neumann said.

    Industry observers note that but investors may be overlooking a key detail about Netflix's business that hasn't changed even as revenue growth slows. Management is highly effective at dialing in content spend and reaching its target operating margin. Operating margin is on track to reach 31.5% this year, up from 29.5% last year.

    It has been revealed that what's more, Netflix's free cash flow conversion is very high and growing. It generated $9.5 billion of free cash flow through the first three quarters of the year. Netflix uses that cash to buy back shares, which supports significant improvements in its earnings per share.

    That's where Ackman believes the current share price makes Netflix stock a compelling buy. "We'll make more money over time if the stock is cheaper in the short- to intermediate-term because they're going to cancel a lot more shares as a result," he noted in a recent interview.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Netflix repurchased $4.8 billion of its stock in the third quarter, and it still has $22.3 billion in authorization capacity. At the tech giant's current share price, the remaining authorization represents around 9% of the current share count.

    Sources indicate that netflix could complete the remaining authorization over the next two years. Management expects to generate about $2.5 billion in free cash flow in the fourth quarter, and that number should steadily climb next year. The organization should be able to maintain its double-digit revenue growth rate for the foreseeable future with improvements in advertising, pricing, and maintaining a low churn rate while operating margin continues to expand. That should result in higher free cash flow conversion, meaning free cash flow grows even faster than earnings.

    In a recent development, ackman and his team project earnings-per-share growth of 19% per year over the next three to five years, driven by Netflix's share repurchase program. The market is pricing Netflix shares at just 22 times its free cash flow, and considering that cash is going right back to shareholders through buybacks, it seems like a fantastic opportunity for investors.

    The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (861 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The debasement trade is gaining latest traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
    • Recent findings suggest that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
    • "The size of the Treasury purchases revealed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining latest traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    Recent findings suggest that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases revealed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    Gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    Recent findings suggest that bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    Recent findings suggest that the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    The Treasury Department stated last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the plans.

    Last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "significant toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Industry observers note that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold stated in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    According to recent reports, the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah mentioned. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    The Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah stated. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    In a recent development, "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah remarked in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Sources indicate that coltman at 21Shares noted the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    Recent findings suggest that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh stated in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    In a recent development, billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

    "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, said Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta Platforms Is Pouring Up to $145 Billion Into AI This Year. Investors Should Watch This 1 Number.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mark Zuckerberg founded Facebook in his Harvard dorm room in 2004.
    • That sort of value creation should force investors to always give Zuckerberg free rein over his vision and how he directs the tech giant's financial resources and talent.
    • Recent findings suggest that it's much harder now to believe that Zuckerberg is following the right strategic path.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:11PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Meta Platforms ›.

    Mark Zuckerberg founded Facebook in his Harvard dorm room in 2004. It didn't take long to grow the social media platform into one of the most powerful technology enterprises on Earth. Called Meta Platforms (META -5.93%) today, it sports a market capitalization of $1.6 trillion.

    That sort of value creation should force investors to always give Zuckerberg free rein over his vision and how he directs the tech giant's financial resources and talent. This is true even though recent blunders, like the metaverse project, haven't panned out. The ”Magnificent Seven” stock is up more than 1,500% since the initial public offering (as of Nov. 17), so his actions have clearly benefited shareholders.

    Recent findings suggest that it's much harder now to believe that Zuckerberg is following the right strategic path. Meta will invest up to $145 billion in capital expenditures (capex) in 2026, with spending likely to be much higher next year. This has turned free cash flow negative and led to a pause in share buybacks.

    In Zuckerberg's mind, it's all about artificial intelligence (AI). Nervous investors need to watch this one number to judge if all this capex is actually worth it.

    Meta's entire business model rests on monetizing the attention of people who interact with its free social media services. It currently has 3.64 billion daily active owners across its family of apps, a gigantic figure that somehow keeps growing. The company makes its money from advertising, which represented 98% of total revenue in Q3 2026.

    According to recent reports, the logical conclusion is that Meta's AI-related spending spree is the right move if it improves advertising metrics. So far, this appears to be the case. This is already a huge business, but the growth has been fantastic.

    Ad revenue rose 25.9% year over year to $63.1 billion in the third quarter. This is just slightly below what Alphabet's (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) Google Search, which is growing at a much slower pace, generated in Q3. Digging deeper, Meta's average price per ad increased 14%, and impressions were up 10%.

    According to recent reports, the ad ecosystem operates like a flywheel, benefiting from a robust network effect. Improving algorithms drive higher user engagement. Data is collected on their interests. Consequently, this attracts advertisers that want to get in front of these people. Meta generates revenue that is reinvested into its technology stack, further reinforcing the feedback loop.

    According to recent reports, AI appears to be strengthening the overall ad ecosystem. On the engagement front, advanced AI models bolster content recommendation. For advertisers, Meta is "leveraging AI to make it easier for businesses to manage campaigns, develop creative, and act on performance opportunities," according to chief financial officer Susan Li.

    The manufacturer has developed and released other AI-related offerings. It sells AI tools to small businesses and enterprises. There is insatiable demand for excess compute, which Meta previously mentioned it can sell at premium prices to outside customers. The popular Muse personal agent can bring in subscription sales and capture commerce revenue share as well. These are immaterial right now, however.

    Industry observers note that advertising is the most important area that investors should watch closely. It's a signal that the hundreds of billions of dollars in capex is driving better financial performance in the core operations. And perhaps most importantly, a thriving ad segment suggests Meta's economic moat is widening.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The AI infrastructure providers get all the love from Wall Street. This includes the chipmakers, cloud platforms, and AI model developers. Their trillion-dollar valuations reflect the market's appreciation.

    But maybe the ultimate winners won't be the companies creating AI. That's an idea worth considering. Most of the value could eventually accrue to businesses that leverage this impressive technology to better serve their customers and improve their lives in unique ways.

    Based on how well its ad machine is working, Meta is doing exactly this.

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 21, 2026 at 11:14PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than SharonAI ›.

    In a recent development, on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 16, 2026, SharonAI (SHAZ -18.06%) introduced an annualized run rate (ARR) revenue metric to track its commercial expansion as data center infrastructure comes online. Commercial execution now determines whether its contractual backing turns into actual cash flow. Three things management said on the call stand out.

    Sources indicate that the manufacturer's annualized run rate revenue, or projected yearly revenue based on active billing, will surge as 30 megawatts of data center power capacity enter active service. That operational activation converts initial infrastructure installations into cash-generating deployments under long-term agreements, with billing expected in January of 2027.

    Rather than tapping high-cost corporate borrowing, management finances graphics processing unit (GPU) hardware using special purpose vehicles (SPVs), or isolated subsidiary companies created for specific infrastructure projects. These debt facilities lock in funding directly against customer agreements where clients must pay regardless of usage.

    In a recent development, customer pricing on multiyear agreements has increased as specialized compute capacity grows scarce across global markets. High contribution margins, or the proportion of revenue remaining after direct operating costs, allow project returns to pay back initial equipment costs well inside contract terms.

    It has been revealed that customers are scrambling for immediate power and compute access, and management is not hiding its satisfaction about its secured data center footprint. The company holds pre-connected power infrastructure in Australia and an anchor partnership with NVIDIA, giving it clear advantages over rivals stuck in utility grid delay queues. Management keeps a close watch on cluster deployment timelines and debt execution.

    Converting a total contract value of $9.6 billion into active billing remains the ultimate test for the business as it ramps hardware deployments into 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026.
    • Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their fresh head coach.
    • The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026.

    Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their fresh head coach.

    The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.

    Frick arrives in the north-east after five years in charge of Luzern, where he transformed the club’s fortunes after taking over in December 2021 with the team rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League. He guided them away from relegation trouble before leading them to a fourth-place finish and qualification for European football.

    Announcing the appointment, Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington mentioned the club had undertaken an extensive recruitment process before selecting Frick as the man to lead the Dons forward.

    Bevington remarked: 'We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club.

    According to recent reports, 'Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

    'Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.'.

    Sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel also welcomed the appointment and believes Frick has the qualities to make a major impact at Pittodrie.

    Pfannenstiel noted: 'Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

    Aberdeen have appointed Mario Frick as their fresh manager.

    'We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact.'.

    Before his spell with Luzern, Frick managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz, winning promotion to the Swiss Super League with the latter. Across almost 290 senior matches as a head coach, he built a reputation for developing young talent, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players.

    It has been revealed that as a player, Frick represented clubs including FC Basel, FC Zürich, St Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana. A striker who could also operate in defence, he won 125 caps for Liechtenstein between 1993 and 2016 and remains his country’s record goalscorer with 16 international goals.

    Frick said: 'I’m excited to be joining Aberdeen FC. It’s a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and massive ambitions.

    'Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.'.

    Frick and assistant coach Matter are expected to arrive in Aberdeen at the start of the week and will begin preparations for next weekend’s Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

    Top Wall Street analysts recommend these 3 dividend stocks for higher returns

    📅 13 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that dividend-paying stocks can enhance portfolio returns by providing a steady income stream to investors and the potential for capital appreciation.
    • In this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, backed by strong financials and cash flows to support consistent dividend payments.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that dividend-paying stocks can enhance portfolio returns by providing a steady income stream to investors and the potential for capital appreciation. Several investors seek exposure to dividend stocks in a volatile backdrop to ensure stable income.

    In this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, backed by strong financials and cash flows to support consistent dividend payments.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Sources indicate that energy Transfer (ET) is a diversified midstream energy firm with about 140,000 miles of pipelines and associated energy infrastructure in 44 states. The company made a quarterly cash distribution of 34 cents per common unit for the second quarter of 2026. At an annualized payment of $1.36 per common unit, ET offers a yield of 6.3%.

    It has been revealed that recently, JPMorgan analyst Jeremy Tonet reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer stock and slightly raised his price target to $25 from $24. The analyst noted that the organization delivered a strong Q2 beat across all key metrics.

    It has been revealed that tonet highlighted that Energy Transfer raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8 billion-$19.1 billion from $18.2 billion-$18.6 billion, reflecting robust base results and cost optimization. The 5-star analyst added that the company "tightened" its capex to $5.6 billion–$5.9 billion and expects capex above $5 billion annually through 2029, given solid opportunities.

    About the Hugh Brinson pipeline, Tonet noted Phase 1 (1.5 bcfd) reaching full capacity by September 1 and Phase II capacity (0.7 bcfd) going online by Q1 2027. The analyst also noted completion of a 14-mile Hugh Brinson lateral in Abilene, Texas, and final stages of talks for an additional 250 mmcfd of Oklahoma power plant demand.

    "All in, we see ET well positioned to continue capitalizing on organic growth opportunities across the value chain," said Tonet.

    Tonet ranks No. 922 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 9%. See Energy Transfer Financials on TipRanks.

    It has been revealed that this week's second dividend pick is independent oil and natural gas company Permian Resources (PR). The company declared a base dividend of $0.16 per share for the third quarter, payable on September 30, 2026. At an annualized dividend of $0.64 per share, PR offers a yield of about 2.7%.

    Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Permian Resources stock and increased his price target to $27 from $22, citing an improved outlook on oil production growth and operational efficiencies.

    Industry observers note that the 5-star analyst noted that while PR stock has outperformed its peers so far in 2026, he sees further upside. Mehta is confident about the organization's operational improvements and ability to deliver incremental free cash flow per share through the strategic ground game program. He added that the program has completed about $1.05 billion in bolt-on deals this year (as of August 5).

    "We see the continued success of PR's ground game as constructive toward future inventory replenishment and increasing working interest over time," mentioned Mehta.

    The analyst also emphasized Permian Resources' solid track record of generating growth in free cash flow (FCF) per share. Mehta expects the company's free cash flow per share to grow at a 20% CAGR (compound annual growth rate) from 2025–2028.

    Industry observers note that mehta ranks No. 401 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.8%. See Permian Resources Statistics on TipRanks.

    In a recent development, moving on to Sempra Energy (SRE), a utility holding company. Earlier this month, the company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.6575 per share, payable on October 15. At an annualized dividend of $2.63 per share, SRE stock offers a yield of about 3.1%.

    It has been revealed that recently, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith upgraded SRE stock to Buy from Hold but slightly lowered the price target to $97 from $101. The 5-star analyst noted that Sempra stock is trading at a price/earnings multiple that is 14% below its electric peers due to concerns about Texas transmission capital expenditure and the failure of California legislation.

    Smith noted that the derating of weaker California peers PG&E (PCG) and Edison International (EIX) is weighing on the sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) valuation but is becoming less relevant given their materially higher fire risk compared to Sempra Energy.

    Furthermore, Smith expects Sempra Energy's Texas capex strategy to stay in place despite the opposition to transmission and data centers, though delays to 765-kV projects are likely. While a full recovery for SRE stock will need a clearer outcome from the Texas legislative session, Smith believes that the stock may already be an early opportunity for patient investors.

    "We are early on the upgrade but see limited downside at current levels as the market is pricing in little transmission upside," remarked Smith.

    In a recent development, smith ranks No. 945 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.2%. See Sempra ETF Exposure on TipRanks.
